full_judgment: 2. Facts leading to filing of this civil appeal, in short, are that the respondents herein as writ petitioners filed writ petition being Writ Petition No.3630 of 1999 before the High Court Division for release/de-requisition of unused land of 6.24 acres of Mouza Foidabad of Cadastral Survey (in short C.C.) Plot Nos.694, 696, 1071, 802, 951, 954, 824, 826, 950, 952 and 1070 and direction for payment of compensation of used land measuring 9.91 acres of Mouza Foidabad of C.S. Plot Nos.788, 965, 877, 948, 811, 806, 867, 870, 880, 811, 829, 835, 827, 839, 840, 841, 844, 845, 847, 852, 862, 863, 864, 879, 884, 842, 843, 847, 848, 861, 863, 879, 881, 807, and 778 which was requisitioned in L.A. Case No.8/64 65 and in L.A. Case No.66/57-58 for development of Uttara Model Town stating, inter alia, that they are the heirs of the C.S. recorded tenant Probhat Ali and Darbesh Ali who were the owners of the total land measuring an area of 16.15 acres of land in Foidabad Mouza within the District Dhaka, and became the owners of the said land by inheritance, purchase and also by way of amicable partition. The writ-respondent Nos.5 and 6 requisitioned the huge area including the above lands in L.A. Case No.66/1957-58 and L.A. Case No.8/64-65 of Dhaka Collectorate under section 93A of the Town Improvement Act, 1952 (E.P. Act No. XIII of 1953) for creating a residential area named Uttara Model Town. Further case of the writ-petitioners is that statutory notices were not served upon the predecessor of the writ-petitioners or upon the writ petitioners, no compensation was paid to the predecessor of the writ petitioners or to the writ petitioners and more-so, the lands covered by the aforesaid plots were not published in the Gazette. The power of attorney holder of the writ petitioners sent a letter on 26.08.1999 to the Manager (Administration) Bangladesh Forms and Publications office, Tejgaon, Dhaka asking him to know whether those plots were published in the Gazette or not, the said Manager replied on 06.09.1999 that the said plots were not published in the Gazette. The requiring body i.e., writ-respondent No.3 took possession of the land of L.A. Case except the plot Nos.694, 696, 1071, 802, 951, 955, 824, 826, 950, 952 and 1070, the writ petitioners are in possession thereof by erecting shops since the time of their predecessors. The writ respondent No.3 neither took possession of the lands in question nor the same was developed for the purpose of establishing of Uttara Model Town for which the lands were acquired. It was alleged in the writ petition that all of a sudden on 7.3.1999 the Duty Officer of Uttara Police Station served a notice upon the writ petitioners and to their power of attorney holder Md. Mukarram Hossain under section 160 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to remove their shops and houses from the scheduled land. Thereafter, on receipt of the said notice on 18.03.1999, a legal notice was served upon the writ-respondent No.3 stating that the scheduled land were not legally requisitioned, as such, appropriate action is required to be taken against the aforesaid L.A. Cases. It was further alleged that thereafter, the power of attorney holder Md. Mukarram Hossain on behalf of all the writ petitioners on 01-07-1999 filed two applications before the writ-respondent No.5 praying for compensation money for the lands which was used and for lease of the lands which was in possession of the writ petitioners and on inquiry Md. Mukarram Hossain, the power of attorney holder of the writ petitioners came to know that a meeting of the Ministry of Land, section 10, Government of Bangladesh, was held on 2.6.1988 and it is revealed from the serial Nos. 13 and 31 of the proceedings of the said meeting, the Government has decided that the land must be used within 3 (three) years from the 'date of acquisition and further decided that 3 katha of plot will be allotted to the affected family but about 11 years have been elapsed without executing the said resolution. The said Mukarram Hossain also inquired into the office of writ-respondent No.3 and found that the RAJUK has decided to sale in auction the lands in question to the highest bidder after developing the said lands as commercial plots, thus, C.S. recorded tenant moved Writ Petition No.7019 of 1997 before the High Court Division where the RAJUK filed an affidavit-in-opposition stating that they will sell those lands after developing the lands. The alleged acquisition took place on 23.09.1965 but land in questions have not been utilized more than 35 years, as such, it is presumed that the requiring body is not in need of the said unutilized land for the purpose of which it was acquisitioned, as such, it is liable to be derequisitioned. The aforesaid L.A. Case is ultra vires of the provision of section 93(A)(4)(h) of the Town Improvement Act, 1953. The writ petitioners further case is that no compensation money has ever been paid to the writ-petitioners or to their predecessor-ininterest tall today, as such, the L.A. case is liable to be declared as without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect. The writ petitioner further stated that on 30.10.1984, the Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms expressed their views that the lands which were purportedly acquired but not used by the requiring body till today should be given back to the owners and the same cannot be kept unused for indefinite period. On the basis of the aforesaid decision of the Government a circular was issued on 02.05.1986 by the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms where it was categorically stated that the purported acquired lands, the possession of which has not been taken by the requiring body should be returned to the owners and according to the aforesaid circular, the Government already returned several hundred unused lands to the previous owners. The writ petitioners further stated that after acquiring the property from the poor people, the RAJUK has sold some of those lands to their employees who developed the same as commercial area and made their fortune. Therefore, the writ petitioners being aggrieved by the aforesaid actions of the writ-respondents and finding no other alternative efficacious remedy moved the above mentioned writ petition before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule Nisi.
